newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midcontinent diesel differentials hold gains.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midcontinent diesel differentials hold gains.

text.p: U.S. Midcontinent diesel fuel differentials in the Group Three market held onto gains generated by strong spot demand and lingering concerns about shipping delays in the region, traders said.
Shipping delays on the Houston-to-Chicago Explorer Pipeline system that were largely ignored earlier in the week emerged as a factor in the market early Friday.

The pipeline system this week said liftings were pushed back by five days by maintenance and a heavy slate of distillate liftings. The pipeline was working to return to its normal schedule by late May.
"I'm not sure why this has suddenly become an issue, but it is," one Midwest trader said of the Explorer delays.
Low sulphur diesel was bid 7.25 cents a gallon over NYMEX May heating oil in Group Three and eased to bids 1.25 cents over the print in Chicago, traders said.
High sulphur was steady at 6.75/7.0 cents over the print in Group Three and eased to 0.75/1.0 cents over the print in Chicago, traders said.
Unleaded gasoline differentials eased to bids 1.50 cents a gallon under NYMEX May unleaded in Group Three and 1.0 cent under the print in Chicago, traders said.
